title: LoL Esports Community Competition Guidelines
summary: LoL Esports Community Competition Guidelines  LoL Esports
content:
We're making it easier than ever to organize League of Legends community competitions. Our updated global guidelines remove outdated restrictions, streamline licensing into a single community competition framework, and reduce restrictions on entry fees, sponsorships, prize pools, and spectator fees. In most cases, organizers will no longer need to wait for Riot approval to run an event. Follow the guidelines, submit your competition through ourvisibility form(pw: riotevent), and start building for your community.

Whether you're organizing a local LAN, a college tournament, or an online bracket, these guidelines are designed to support community competition across the evolving League of Legends experience, including Summoner's Rift, ARAM, Arena, League of Legends Classic, and future experiences.

You're free to organize League of Legends competitions at nearly any scale, whether that's a local LAN at your PC café, a school or university, an online community competition, an open bracket, or a larger invitational event. We want to support community competition across League's growing ecosystem of game modes, including Summoner's Rift, Arena, League Classic, and future experiences.

These guidelines are designed for community organizers operating independently and in good faith. However, some organizations are not covered under this community competition license and will need to work directly with Riot through a separate process.

We know community competitions take time, effort, and resources to run, and we want organizers to have the flexibility to build sustainable events. There are no fixed caps on entry fees, sponsorship revenue, prize pools, or spectator ticketing under these guidelines.

We do ask organizers to act reasonably, provide fair value to players, fans, and partners participating in the event, and avoid misleading or deceptive practices. While we have removed many of the previous restrictions, certain sponsor categories remain off-limits. You can find the full list of restricted sponsors below in the “What types of sponsors should I avoid making agreements with?” section.

title: LoL Esports |
content:
TL;DR- Triumphant Ryze is back! Originally awarded to winners of community competitions, Triumphant Ryze has long been a symbol of League's grassroots competitive spirit. Alongside our updatedCommunity Competition Guidelines, we're bringing the skin back for winners of qualifying community tournaments to celebrate the organizers and players who continue to build League's competitive community around the world.

Community competition has always been part of what makes League of Legends special. Long before packed arenas and international championships, League's competitive scene was built by community tournaments that brought players together, sparked rivalries, and helped launch countless competitive journeys.

To celebrate that legacy, we're excited to announce the return ofTriumphant Ryze.

Historically, Triumphant Ryze was awarded to winners of community and Riot-supported competitions as a symbol of League's grassroots competitive spirit. While distribution of the skin paused several years ago as we worked toward a more consistent global process, we're excited to bring it back as part of our renewed investment in Organized Play.

Triumphant Ryze is reserved for champions.

Players who win qualifying community competitions will once again be eligible to receive one of League's most iconic and recognizable competitive rewards. By reserving the skin for tournament winners, we hope to preserve the prestige that has always made Triumphant Ryze special while giving players another reason to jump into community competition.

title: LoL Amateur and Event Tournaments No Longer Require Riot Approval
summary: LoL Amateur and Event Tournaments No Longer Require Riot Approval  Inven Global
content:
Riot Games has significantly overhauled its community tournament guidelines for League of Legends (LoL), introducing a single, unified framework that applies globally across all regions.

The most significant change in this update is the increased autonomy granted to organizers. The previous requirement for prior approval from Riot Games has been largely abolished; organizers can now freely host Internet cafe LAN tournaments, university tournaments, and online community events simply by submitting a simplified status form.

At the same time, key restrictions have been eased to improve the sustainability of these events. Previous caps on entry fees, sponsorship revenue, total prize pools, and spectator ticket prices have been removed, and limitations on the duration and number of participating schools for university and high school tournaments have also been lifted.

Tournament broadcasts can now be streamed freely on any online platform, and organizers are permitted to charge for viewing or set up pay-per-view options. However, broadcasting via traditional TV channels (linear TV) remains prohibited.

While organizers may use official LoL assets to promote their events, they are strictly prohibited from using official esports branding—such as Riot Games, LCK, or Worlds—in a way that could lead viewers to mistake the event for an official, sponsored tournament. Restrictions on sponsors from harmful sectors, including gambling, cryptocurrency and NFTs, alcohol, tobacco, and political organizations, remain in place.

Riot Games expressed optimism about expanding the grassroots esports ecosystem, stating, "By reducing the burden of approval for organizers, we plan to support promising community tournaments submitted through our forms with various benefits, including promotion and future reward programs."
